content.summary: Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) provides direct visualization of infarcted regions, information on scarring and viability, and can differentiate myocardial infarction from other myocardial injury (e.g. myocarditis). CMR is valuable for diagnosing AMI when uncertainty exists, identifying culprit vascular territory, confirming myocarditis or takotsubo cardiomyopathy, and is the gold standard for assessment of left ventricular (LV) thrombus. CMR can also assess myocardial perfusion with pharmacological stress and may be used as an alternative to coronary CT angiography (CCTA) in the observe zone after ECG and high-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn) assessments, particularly in patients with advanced/established coronary artery disease (CAD). Additional information on CMR, single-photon emission computerized tomography (SPECT) perfusion imaging and stress echocardiography is provided in the supplementary data online.
